caption:
Plus one etiquette for your wedding: what to say when a guest replies for more people than you invited.
Entry 04 of Norah's Notebook: a plus-one policy, envelope wording, and a kind script for the phone call.
Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. The tips are real.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: Plus-one rules in short. Before the envelope: decide your policy. Spouses, engaged partners and live-in partners are invited; a casual date is optional (Emily Post, 2008). "No ring, no bring" is outdated, and one planner says the wedding party gets a plus-one unless money is very tight (WeddingWire, 2020). Apply your rule fairly (Zola, 2025). On the envelope: name every seat you mean, and write "and family" only when you mean it (Emily Post, 2008; Zola, 2026). After the envelope: if an extra name arrives, call, and blame the venue or the budget, never the guest (Emily Post, 2008). Copy, paste, say: "We'd love to have you, but our invitation is for the four of you." Fiction: Mara, Eli, Dana and Norah are invented; the tips are real. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: What's your plus-one rule: partners only, or everyone?

sources.fact: Spouses, fiance(e)s and live-in partners must be invited, including to the rehearsal dinner; dating partners who do not live together need not be
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

sources.fact: 'No ring, no bring' is outdated; decide plus-ones case by case; planner Mindy Weiss says wedding-party members should get a plus-one unless money is very tight
sources.title: 5 Plus-One Wedding Etiquette Rules Couples MUST Follow

sources.fact: Limit plus-ones to married or long-term couples and apply the rule fairly
sources.title: Who Has a Say in the Wedding Guest List?

sources.fact: Wedding invitations are not negotiations; the inner envelope is the final word on who exactly is being invited; 'and family' covers household members under the same roof
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

sources.fact: To signal no plus-one, write only the invited guest's name on the envelope; for families, 'X and X and Family'
sources.title: Wedding Invitation Wording: A Complete How-To Guide

sources.fact: Call to correct an extra reply and stick to your guns; couples can decline extra guests by citing venue size or budget
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

needs_proof: T77 and T23 rest on a 2008 Emily Post column (r2 notes that current wording may differ); the year is shown on screen.
The wedding-party line comes from one planner quoted by WeddingWire (2020); it is attributed as 'a planner says', not stated as a rule.
claims_review.notes: No statistics are used. Story numbers (six weeks, a reply for six, an invitation for four) are invented and never presented as results. The call-to-correct advice in T77 is written for uninvited children; here it is applied to extra adult names, which is the same principle (the envelope is the final word). The door-day advice from T77 (welcome extra guests, ask the caterer for plates) is deliberately left to the Copy, Paste, Send episode on late replies and extra people. The product appears only as two S04 beats, roughly eight seconds, in the brand's voice: the couple sets a plus-one allowance per guest and the reply form asks for plus-one names up to that number (r3 B1). No claim that it prevents surprise replies. The quoted line is Norah's suggested wording adapted from the r2 suggested wording.
